faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Free PDF tools, privacy and Hindi support — the essentials.
faq.q1: Is DocoPDF really free to use?
faq.a1: Yes. Every tool is free, with no signup, no watermarks and no daily limits. Because most tools run entirely in your browser, they're fast too — your files are processed on your own device, not a distant server.
faq.q2: How do I convert JPG to PDF for free?
faq.a2: Open the JPG to PDF tool, drop your photos (JPG, PNG, WEBP, HEIC and TIFF all work), drag them into the order you want, and click Create PDF. The document is built on your device — nothing is ever uploaded.
faq.q3: How can I convert a PDF to Word or text?
faq.a3: For text, use PDF to Text — it extracts everything on your device and can even read scanned pages with OCR in English or Hindi. A full PDF to Word converter that keeps formatting is on our roadmap.
faq.q4: Are my PDF files uploaded to a server?
faq.a4: No. Almost every tool runs 100% on your device inside the browser — your files never leave your computer or phone, and once the site is loaded most tools keep working even offline.
faq.q5: Can I edit a PDF without Adobe Acrobat?
faq.a5: Yes. Edit PDF gives you a Word-style editor — click existing text to retype it, add images, shapes and signatures, highlight and annotate — free and on your device. Annotate PDF and Write PDF round out the set.
faq.a6: Yes. The whole interface is available in Hindi, and you can write PDFs in Devanagari, fill Hindi forms and OCR scanned documents in Hindi with fully searchable output.

rep.ctaNoObjects: No PDF objects found — nothing to repair
rep.valObjects: {count, plural, =1 {1 recoverable object} other {# recoverable objects}}
rep.valHeaderAt: Header buried at byte {offset} — junk before it will be dropped
rep.valHeaderMissing: No %PDF- header anywhere in the file
rep.valXrefOk: startxref points at a real xref table
rep.valXrefBad: startxref points at the wrong place — offsets are broken
rep.valXrefMissing: No startxref / xref table — the file cannot be indexed
rep.valDups: {count, plural, =1 {1 object number appears twice — the last one wins} other {# object numbers appear more than once — the last one wins}}
rep.encBody: Repairing is not cracking — an encrypted PDF is rejected here so its damage is never "repaired" into unreadable ciphertext. Remove the password with Unlock PDF first, then repair.
rep.noObjectsTitle: No PDF objects in this file
rep.noObjectsBody: The scanner could not find a single "N G obj" pattern — there is no PDF structure left to salvage. This is not a PDF that broke; it never was one.
rep.planScan: Raw byte scan: every "N G obj" object is recovered from wherever it survives in the file, and its extent is closed at the nearest endstream — wrong /Length values are corrected against the real data.
rep.planRebuild: A brand-new cross-reference table, trailer and header are built around the catalog with the most reachable pages — exactly what a viewer needs to open the file.
rep.planRebuildValidOn: If the structure check passes, the file is still rewritten fresh (valid files get the same rebuild).
rep.planRebuildValidOff: A file that passes the structure check is returned byte-for-byte unchanged.
rep.planVerify: Before anything ships, the rebuilt PDF must strict-load with correct object parsing — the reported page count is what that verification sees.
rep.limitsTitle: What repair can and cannot do
rep.limitsBody: Fixes what is structural: broken xref/startxref, junk before the header, wrong stream lengths, duplicate objects, missing %%EOF. Cannot fix what is gone: fonts and images already missing from the bytes stay missing.
rep.limitsTruncated: Truncated files are handled honestly: content past the cut does not exist anymore, so the report flags the truncation and the page count reflects only what survived — pages are never invented.
rep.resTruncated: Truncation detected: the file tail was cut mid-object. Everything after the cut was not in the bytes and could not be recovered — the page count reflects only what survived.
rep.resUnchanged: The structure check passed — the file was already healthy, so it was returned byte-for-byte unchanged.
rep.resValidRebuilt: The structure check passed — the file was healthy and was rewritten with a fresh header, xref and trailer as requested.
rep.doneDesc: {name} downloaded — {pages, plural, =1 {1 page} other {# pages}} verified.
rep.errNoObjects: No PDF objects could be found in this file — there is nothing to repair.
rep.errNoCatalog: Objects were recovered, but no page catalog survived — the file's structure cannot be rebuilt.
rep.errNoPages: A catalog was found, but no complete page is reachable — no honest PDF can be produced.
rep.errVerify: The rebuilt file failed final verification — the damage was too severe to repair honestly.

wpdf.pipeTitle: Where does my page actually go?
wpdf.pipeBody: Nowhere permanent — that is the honest split. Browsers cannot fetch other sites directly, so our own server fetches the HTML as a dumb pipe and hands it straight to your browser: it is never stored, logged or forwarded. The PDF itself is rendered entirely on your device, in a Web Worker, with the same engine as HTML to PDF. Internal addresses (127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x …) are refused outright.
wpdf.pasteTitle: Already saved the page as a file?
wpdf.pasteBody: Browser-saved “Web page, complete” files and hand-written HTML never need the fetch pipe at all —
wpdf.honestNote: Honest limits: this renders the page's server HTML — no JavaScript, no CSS layout, no images (alt text prints in brackets); SPA shells and paywalled pages may carry little content; Hindi text renders through the embedded Noto Devanagari subset (bold falls back to regular).

vei.how1: Drop a CII e-invoice XML file, or a PDF with an embedded Factur-X/ZUGFeRD XML — the tool detects which arrived, entirely on your device.
vei.how2: Read the verdict — fourteen concrete checks with chips: structure, date, type code, seller/buyer, line items and the three totals cross-checks.
vei.how3: Fix what the checklist points at, then download the plain-text validation report with the actual vs expected numbers.
vei.ctaUnknown: This is neither an XML nor a PDF file
vei.modeXmlBody: The file starts like an XML document — it will be parsed and validated directly.
vei.modePdfBody: The embedded Factur-X/ZUGFeRD XML will be extracted (factur-x.xml, zugferd-invoice.xml, or any embedded .xml) and validated.
vei.limitsTitle: What this check is — and is not
vei.limitsChecked: Checked: root element, document context + guideline, invoice number, issue date, type code, seller/buyer names, line items with net amounts, the three totals cross-checks (±0.01), tax categories + rates, ISO 4217 currency, and (for Factur-X PDFs) the XMP conformance claim vs the XML's completeness — informational.
vei.limitsNot: Not checked: full XSD schema validation (too heavy to bundle — this is a structural + EN 16931-flavored semantic check, not schema validation), signature / e-seal verification, and any business rules beyond the checks listed. A PASS means the listed checks passed.
vei.verdictPassBody: Every listed check passed. This means the structural + semantic rules this tool checks are satisfied — not that the invoice is flawless in every legal respect.
vei.verdictWarnBody: Nothing failed, but some checks raised warnings — open the rows to see what is missing or unusual before you send the invoice out.
vei.verdictFailBody: At least one check failed — open the red rows to see the actual vs expected values. A receiver will most likely reject this file.
vei.sourcePdf: Embedded XML extracted from the PDF: {name}
vei.sourceXml: The XML file was validated directly
vei.errNotXml: This file is neither a PDF nor an XML document — there is nothing to validate here.
vei.errNoAttachment: This PDF has no embedded XML attachment (no Factur-X/ZUGFeRD XML was found) — only page text, which cannot be validated as an e-invoice.
vei.errXmlParse: The XML could not be parsed at all — it is not well-formed enough to read.
vei.errTooBig: The XML is larger than the 20 MB sanity limit — this is not a normal e-invoice.
vei.title: e-invoice validation report
vei.generatedBy: Generated on-device by DocoPDF — nothing was uploaded.
vei.honestyBody: This is a structural + EN 16931-flavored semantic check, not a full XSD schema validation, not a signature/e-seal verification, and not a complete business-rule validation. The checks above are the whole scope.
vei.kGrand: GrandTotal == TaxBasis + sum of tax amounts
vei.nUbl: This looks like a UBL invoice (root <Invoice>), not CII — the CII checks will mostly fail.
vei.nNoGuideline: ExchangedDocumentContext is present but carries no GuidelineSpecifiedDocumentContextParameter/ID.
vei.nDateIso: Extended ISO form accepted; CII canonically uses format 102 (YYYYMMDD).
vei.nTypeUnknown: Numeric code present, but not in the common UNTDID 1001 set this tool knows.
vei.nNameless: Some line items have no SpecifiedTradeProduct/Name.
vei.nLineNetBad: Some line net amounts are missing or not dot-decimal numbers.
vei.nSumViaLt: TaxBasisTotalAmount is missing; verified against the header LineTotalAmount instead.
vei.nNoParseableNets: No line net amount parsed — the sum could not really be verified.
vei.nBasisMissing: GrandTotal could not be cross-checked without TaxBasisTotalAmount.
vei.nNoTaxEntries: No ApplicableTradeTax entries exist — grand total was verified against an empty tax sum.
vei.nDueMissing: DuePayableAmount is not present — the final payable amount is not stated.
vei.nTaxBad: Some ApplicableTradeTax entries have unknown categories or unparseable rates/amounts.
vei.nCurrencyRare: Three-letter code outside the common whitelist — it may be a rarer valid ISO 4217 code.
vei.nConfMismatch: The PDF's XMP claims a higher profile than the XML's contents show (informational, not a verdict).
vei.nConfInsufficient: The XML lacks even MINIMUM completeness (lines + totals), so the claim could not be assessed.
vei.nConfUnknown: Unrecognized XMP ConformanceLevel value (informational, not a verdict).
vei.nConfLower: The claim is at or below what the XML contains — consistent (informational, not a verdict).

vps.title: PDF signature verification report
vps.iTampered: TAMPERED — content differs from what was signed
vps.empty: No signature fields found — this PDF carries no digital signature.
vps.nByteRangeBad: The /ByteRange entry is missing or malformed — the covered byte ranges cannot be established.
vps.nRangeBounds: The /ByteRange entries point outside the file.
vps.nContentsBad: The /Contents entry is not a valid hex string — the CMS signature container cannot be read.
vps.nCmsBad: The CMS (PKCS#7 SignedData) could not be parsed from /Contents.
vps.nNoSigner: The CMS contains no SignerInfo — nobody actually signed.
vps.nNoSidCert: The signer's certificate was not found in the signature's certificate set — the signature could not be cryptographically verified.
vps.nUnsupportedDigest: The digest algorithm is outside this tool's set (SHA-1/256/384/512) — integrity could not be recomputed.
vps.nModified: Bytes were added after the signature's covered ranges end — the file was modified after signing.
vps.nSelfSigned: The certificate is self-signed: cryptographically valid, but not chained to any trusted authority (none was checked).
vps.nExpired: The certificate's validity window has ended at the time of checking.
vps.nNotYetValid: The certificate was not yet valid at the time of checking.
vps.nWeakDigest: SHA-1 digest — processed, but considered weak for new signatures.
vps.nSignTimeOutside: The claimed signing time lies outside the certificate's validity window.
vps.nTimeMismatch: The PDF /M time and the signedAttrs signingTime disagree.
vps.nGapMismatch: The /Contents position does not line up with the /ByteRange gap — unusual producer.
vps.nFrontGap: The first byte range does not start at 0 — leading bytes are not covered by the signature.
vps.nAttached: The CMS is not detached — its integrity relationship to the PDF bytes cannot be checked by digest comparison.
vps.nNoSignedAttrs: No signedAttrs in the SignerInfo — the messageDigest integrity check is unavailable (the signature covers the content directly).
vps.nVerifyError: WebCrypto could not process the signature (unsupported key type or encoding).
vps.generatedBy: Generated on-device by DocoPDF — nothing was uploaded.
vps.honestyBody: No CRL/OCSP revocation check, no chain-of-trust validation, no timestamp (TSA) verification and no PAdES long-term validation were performed — there is no trust store on this device to check against. A self-signed certificate shows as untrusted-but-valid. A verdict of VALID means exactly: the signature verifies cryptographically, the signed byte ranges are intact and the coverage is complete — nothing more.

vps.toneAttentionBody: The signatures are cryptographically sound, but something deserves a look — read the notes on each card.

ds.how1: Drop the PDF and pick your .pfx/.p12 certificate — both stay on your device and are never uploaded.
ds.how2: Type the certificate password and check the signer summary, then set the reason, location, page and position.
ds.how3: Press Sign — a worker seals the document with a real PAdES signature (and a visible block if you want one).

pa.how1: Drop the PDF and pick the conformance target — PDF/A-1b, 2b or 3b. The file stays on your device.
pa.how2: Press Convert — a worker embeds or substitutes fonts, rewrites device colors to DeviceRGB and strips JavaScript and multimedia.
pa.how3: Download the converted PDF together with the plain-text change report that says exactly what was done.
pa.ctaUnknown: This does not look like a PDF — nothing to convert.
pa.modePdfBody: Ready for conversion — fonts, colors, forbidden content and metadata will be handled per the level you pick below.
pa.riskEncrypted: Encrypted — PDF/A forbids it, the run will be refused
pa.riskJs: JavaScript found — it will be removed
pa.riskTransparency: Transparency found — allowed at 2b/3b, refused at 1b
pa.riskEmbedded: Embedded files — dropped at 1b/2b, kept at 3b
pa.riskNote: This is a quick byte-level sniff of the open file; the conversion itself walks the real structure. Compressed streams can hide things — the worker's walk is the authority.
pa.targetHint: Not sure? Pick 2b — the balanced level most archives accept. 1b is the strictest, 3b additionally allows embedded files (how Factur-X invoices are archived).
pa.t1bHint: 2005 · the strictest: no transparency, no embedded files; the standard-14 fonts may stay unembedded.
pa.t2bHint: 2011 · the balanced default: transparency allowed; standard-14 fonts get embedded substitutes.
pa.t3bHint: 2012 · like 2b plus embedded files (Factur-X/ZUGFeRD archival level).
pa.limitsTitle: What this tool honestly does not do
pa.limitsBody: It produces the -b (basic) levels only — no tagging or structure tree is added (that is the -a, accessible, level). The change report lists everything that was actually done; it is not a certified ISO 19005 validation. Run the result through Validate PDF/A for an independent on-device check.
pa.privacyLine: The document is loaded, rewritten and saved inside a worker thread on your device — nothing is uploaded. Only this site's own substitute font files are fetched, never your data.

vpa.how1: Drop a PDF — the file is read entirely on your device, never uploaded.
vpa.how2: Pick PDF/A-1b, -2b or -3b — or Auto to take the level from the file's XMP — and press Check.
vpa.how3: Read the grouped pass/fail/warning cards with page references, then download the plain-text report.

vpa.modePdfBody: The conformance checks run on this device, straight from the raw bytes.
vpa.limitsBody: A veraPDF-inspired honest subset of ISO 19005 — roughly 15 rule families: identification, fonts, colour, transparency, forbidden content, structure and metadata mirroring. A COMPLIANT verdict means every check in this subset passed — not a certified validation. The PDF/UA rows are advisory hints only.
vpa.levelHint: Auto reads the level from the file's own XMP identification.
vpa.tonePassBody: Every check in this tool's rule subset passed. This is a strong signal, not a certification — archive-grade acceptance still belongs to a certified validator.
vpa.toneWarnBody: No rule failed, but some findings deserve a look — the OutputIntent and /Info↔XMP mirror checks are warning-level on purpose.
vpa.toneFailBody: At least one rule failed. Read the red cards — each one says what was found, where, and what the level requires.
vpa.assumedLine: No XMP identification found — checked against PDF/A-{level} (assumed)
vpa.mismatchLine: The XMP claims {claim} while the checks ran against {level}.
vpa.recoveryLine: Recovered by linear object scan — the xref chain was unusable.
vpa.uaHonesty: These three rows are light accessibility hints, not PDF/UA validation — they never affect the PDF/A verdict.
vpa.title: PDF/A conformance report (honest subset)
vpa.nXmpNone: The catalog carries no readable /Metadata stream — a PDF/A file must identify itself in XMP.
vpa.nXmpNoPart: XMP metadata is present but has no pdfaid:part identification — the file does not claim PDF/A.
vpa.nXmpMismatch: The XMP pdfaid:part/conformance does not match the declared level.
vpa.nXmpConfMismatch: The XMP conformance letter differs from the declared level (a stricter letter is a nuance, not a violation).
vpa.nXmpOk: The file identifies itself as PDF/A in XMP, matching the target level.
vpa.nTitleSkip: No XMP metadata — the title check has nothing to read.
vpa.nTitleOk: dc:title is present in the XMP.
vpa.nTitleWarn: dc:title is missing from the XMP (recommended, not required).
vpa.nFontsNone: No fonts are used by the page content — nothing to embed.
vpa.nFontsOk: Every font used by page content is embedded.
vpa.nFontsStd14: Only standard-14 fonts are unembedded, which PDF/A-1b allows.
vpa.nFontsFail: Unembedded fonts are used by page content — this level requires embedding.
vpa.nCmykOk: No device CMYK found in content streams or resources.
vpa.nCmykOps: Device CMYK operators (k/K) found in content streams.
vpa.nTransOk1b: No transparency found — required at PDF/A-1b.
vpa.nTransFail1b: Transparency (/SMask, groups, soft masks) is forbidden at PDF/A-1b.
vpa.nTransOk2b: Transparency is present and allowed at this level.
vpa.nTransOkNone: No transparency found in the document.
vpa.nPsFail: PostScript calculator functions (/FunctionType 4) are forbidden in PDF/A.
vpa.nJsFail: JavaScript found (/Names/JavaScript or /JS actions) — forbidden in PDF/A.
vpa.nOaOk: /OpenAction is a destination, as PDF/A requires.
vpa.nOaFail: /OpenAction is an action dictionary — PDF/A requires the destination form.
vpa.nEmbOk12: No embedded files — as PDF/A-1b/2b require.
vpa.nEmbOk3: Embedded files are allowed at PDF/A-3b.
vpa.nMmFail: Multimedia annotations found — forbidden in PDF/A.
vpa.nOiOk: An OutputIntent with an ICC profile stream is present.
vpa.nOiWarn: No OutputIntent with an ICC profile — many honest producers omit it (warning, not a failure).
vpa.nStructAOk: MarkInfo/Marked and StructTreeRoot are present, as level-a conformance requires.
vpa.nStructAFail: Level-a conformance requires MarkInfo/Marked and a structure tree.
vpa.nMirrorSkip: No XMP metadata to mirror against.
vpa.nMirrorOk: The /Info entries are mirrored by the XMP (light check: Title/Author/Keywords/Producer).
vpa.nMirrorWarn: Some /Info entries are not mirrored by the XMP.
vpa.nUaMarkedFail: MarkInfo /Marked is not true — PDF/UA requires a tagged document.
vpa.nUaAltOk: Alternate text entries found in the structure tree.
vpa.nUaAltWarn: No /Alt entries found in the structure tree (light scan).
vpa.nUaAltFail: No structure tree — no /Alt scan possible.

vpa.honestyBody: This is an honest subset of ISO 19005 rule families, inspired by veraPDF's categories — not the full standard and not a certified validation. Roughly 15 rule families are checked; a COMPLIANT verdict means every check in this subset passed, nothing more. The PDF/UA rows are advisory hints only (full PDF/UA validation is not performed). Take archive-grade decisions to a certified validator.
